scope.flow: ERC-4337 UserOp signature validation in AtomWallet._validateSignature
scope.environment: AtomWallet ERC-4337 smart account with OpenZeppelin ECDSA.tryRecover

statements.text: A valid on-chain ECDSA signature from an AtomWallet owner is observable after any executed UserOp.
An adversary can derive a high-s counterpart of a valid owner signature via s' = secp256k1_order - s and v' = v XOR 1, whose recovered address is identical to the original signer.
The adversary submits a griefing UserOp carrying the derived high-s signature targeting an AtomWallet.
In _validateSignature, the InvalidSignatureS branch unconditionally reverts instead of returning SIG_VALIDATION_FAILED, so validateUserOp reverts on the high-s signature.
When bundlers simulate the griefing UserOp, validateUserOp reverts, wasting bundler compute on every griefing submission.
If the bundler's error handling does not distinguish a wallet revert from a transient failure, it may retry or blacklist the wallet.
In EntryPoint implementations where validation reverts propagate to the outer handleOps call, the bundler's entire batch transaction fails on-chain, causing gas loss.
Persistent griefing can cause bundlers to deprioritize or refuse to service the targeted AtomWallet, degrading the user's ability to submit transactions through ERC-4337 infrastructure.
On signature mismatch, validateUserOp SHOULD return SIG_VALIDATION_FAILED (1) without reverting, so the EntryPoint can distinguish a signature failure from a wallet bug.

ambiguities: Report does not state whether the griefing UserOp was actually observed on-chain; effects are described as potential/conditional.
Report does not specify which EntryPoint version or bundler implementation is in scope for the batch-failure effect.
Report does not quantify gas loss or compute waste amounts.
